hints: Differentiate using the chain rule, multiplying by $3$ for each term.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the sign of $f'(x)$ for the domain $x > 2$:
$$x > 2 \implies 3x - 6 > 0 \implies (3x - 6)^3 > 0 \text{ and } (3x - 6)^4 > 0$$
$$f'(x) = -\left[\frac{24}{(3x - 6)^3} + \frac{9}{(3x - 6)^4}\right] < 0$$
Conclude that $f$ is a decreasing function for all $x > 2$.

hints: A strictly monotonic function is one-to-one and therefore has an inverse.
walkthrough:
State the existence and reason:
$$f^{-1} \text{ exists because } f \text{ is strictly decreasing (a one-to-one function) for all } x > 2.$$

hints: Evaluate the lower limit as $x \to a$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the range of the linear function $g(x) = 4x - 3$ for $x > a$:
$$\text{Range of } g:\quad g(x) > 4a - 3\quad\left(\text{or } (4a - 3, \infty)\right)$$

hints: Set the lower bound of the range of $g$ ($4a - 3$) $\ge 2$.
walkthrough:
State the condition for the composite function $fg$ to exist:
$$\text{Range of } g \subseteq \text{Domain of } f$$

Set up the inequality with $\text{Domain of } f = (2, \infty)$:
$$4a - 3 \ge 2 \implies 4a \ge 5 \implies a \ge \frac{5}{4}\quad\left(\text{or } a > \frac{5}{4}\right)$$
